efile.text: You must file returns and pay withholding taxes electronically if: you're a new business or existing business applying for an additional registration; you're a payroll service provider (third-party bulk filer); you're an employer/business with an annual combined tax liability of $5,000 or more tallied from among withholding, sales/use and certain excise taxes. Any return indicating "0" tax due must be e-filed through MassTaxConnect.

returns.name: Form M-941, Employer's Return of Income Taxes Withheld
contents: Annual filers: return and payment by January 31 of the following year; quarterly: on or before the last day of the month after the quarter; monthly: on or before the 15th day of the following month (March, June, September and December wages by the last day of the following month); over $25,000: quarterly returns through MassTaxConnect with payments on the quarter-monthly schedule.

A return must be filed even if no tax is due; one period per return; a return showing zero must be e-filed in MassTaxConnect; paper returns and payments count as timely when postmarked at least two days before the due date.
Electronically filed returns are timely if submitted before 12 a.m. Eastern on the due date.

returns.name: Form M-3 (or M-3M), Reconciliation of Massachusetts Income Taxes Withheld, with Forms W-2
contents: Paper Forms W-2 and the reconciliation Form M-3 or M-3M are filed on or before February 28 following the end of the calendar year.

Employers with 50 or more employees file Forms W-2 in machine-readable form (file upload through MassTaxConnect or electronic data transfer) by the last day of March for the preceding year; employees get their W-2 by January 31 (a fine of up to $1,000 applies otherwise).
The quarterly wage reports (Department of Unemployment Assistance) and new-hire reports (within 2 weeks) are separate.

deposits.interpretation: Massachusetts sets the filing frequency from the employer's PROJECTED annual withholding: $100 or less ANNUAL (Form M-941, return and payment by January 31 of the new year); $101 to $1,200 QUARTERLY (by the last day of the month after the quarter); $1,201 to $25,000 MONTHLY (by the 15th of the following month, except wages of March, June, September and December, due the last day of the following month); MORE than $25,000 (the large-employer, accelerated schedule): quarterly returns through MassTaxConnect by the last day of the month after the quarter, with payments on a deposit schedule: when the Massachusetts tax withheld and not yet paid is $500 or more at the end of a quarter-monthly period (the 7th, 15th, 22nd or last day of the month), it must be paid within 3 business days after that period; whatever is below $500 at quarter end is paid with the quarterly return. A late deposit by a large employer draws a 5% penalty. INTERPRETATION: the $500 test is applied to the amount withheld and not previously paid over, carried forward and restarted each quarter (the Guide says: 'When Massachusetts income tax withheld is $500 or more by the 7th, 15th, 22nd and last day of a month, pay over within 3 business days after that'). The frequency is an INPUT (the Department assigns it from the projected figure) or is derived from a supplied projected annual withholding. A return showing zero must still be e-filed in MassTaxConnect.

enrollment: Employers must register with the Department before filing returns and making payments electronically (MassTaxConnect).

Payroll service providers (third-party bulk filers) must file and pay electronically; a third-party service agent uploads W-2 reports through its MassTaxConnect account (stored W-2 specifications, Rev. 20191219).

returns.name: Quarterly unemployment insurance contribution and wage report
contents: Contributions are due and payable on the last day of the first month succeeding the quarter (April 30, July 31, October 31, January 31) (430 CMR 5.03(4)).

All employers file the quarterly contribution report electronically in the form and manner the Commissioner prescribes (430 CMR 5.03(4)(d)). For payroll processing services paying by electronic funds transfer, the payment must be credited by the statutory due date and a Saturday, Sunday or legal holiday moves it to the next succeeding business day (5.03(13)(d)).
Non-profit and governmental employers paying in lieu of contributions file a quarterly wage and employment report due the same day (430 CMR 5.06(5)).

notModelled: The regulation states the Saturday, Sunday and legal-holiday rule only for payroll processing services' electronic payments (5.03(13)(d)); the same next-business-day rule is applied to every employer's report and payment, which the text read does not state.
